+package org.openjdk.jmc.flightrecorder.internal.parser;
+
+/**
+ * Converts the ticks in a chunk to nanoseconds. Both timestamps and timespans are converted with
+ * this when parsed, so that every time value of a recording is held in nanoseconds and derived
+ * values, such as an end time computed as start time plus duration, use exact long arithmetic.
+ */
+public final class TicksConverter {
+	private static final long NANOS_PER_SECOND = 1_000_000_000L;
+
+	private final double ticksPerNano;
+	// Zero unless a tick is a whole number of nanoseconds
+	private final long nanosPerTick;
+	private final long maxExactTicks;
+
+	/**
+	 * @param ticksPerSecond
+	 *            the tick frequency of the chunk
+	 */
+	public TicksConverter(long ticksPerSecond) {
+		ticksPerNano = ticksPerSecond / (double) NANOS_PER_SECOND;
+		nanosPerTick = (ticksPerSecond > 0 && NANOS_PER_SECOND % ticksPerSecond == 0)
+				? NANOS_PER_SECOND / ticksPerSecond : 0;
+		maxExactTicks = nanosPerTick == 0 ? 0 : Long.MAX_VALUE / nanosPerTick;
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * @param ticks
+	 *            the number of ticks to convert, relative to the chunk start
+	 * @return the number of nanoseconds
+	 */
+	public long toNanos(long ticks) {
+		if (nanosPerTick != 0 && ticks <= maxExactTicks && ticks >= -maxExactTicks) {
+			return ticks * nanosPerTick;
+		}
+		return (long) (ticks / ticksPerNano);
+	}
+
+	/**
+	 * @param ticks
+	 *            a fractional number of ticks, relative to the chunk start
+	 * @return the number of nanoseconds, scaled before truncating towards zero
+	 */
+	public long toNanos(double ticks) {
+		return (long) (nanosPerTick != 0 ? ticks * nanosPerTick : ticks / ticksPerNano);
+	}
+}

+package org.openjdk.jmc.flightrecorder.internal.parser.v0;
+
+import org.openjdk.jmc.common.unit.IQuantity;
+import org.openjdk.jmc.common.unit.UnitLookup;
+import org.openjdk.jmc.flightrecorder.internal.parser.TicksConverter;
+import org.openjdk.jmc.flightrecorder.internal.parser.v0.model.DataType;
+
+/**
+ * Reads a timespan in ticks as nanoseconds, converted the same way as tick timestamps, so that a
+ * start time plus a duration is computed exactly.
+ */
+class TicksTimespanReader extends QuantityReader {
+	private final TicksConverter ticksConverter;
+
+	TicksTimespanReader(DataType dataType, TicksConverter ticksConverter) {
+		super(dataType, UnitLookup.NANOSECOND);
+		this.ticksConverter = ticksConverter;
+	}
+
+	@Override
+	IQuantity quantity(long numericalValue) {
+		return UnitLookup.NANOSECOND.quantity(ticksConverter.toNanos(numericalValue));
+	}
+
+	@Override
+	IQuantity quantity(double numericalValue) {
+		return UnitLookup.NANOSECOND.quantity(ticksConverter.toNanos(numericalValue));
+	}
+}
